clue.text: Jazz legend's hit with "Apple Girl"

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the legend is what the letters make

indicators.note: hit suggests the letters are knocked about and scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A famous jazz musician scores a chart success with a song called Apple Girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' looks like a chart success, but it tells you to rearrange the letters of APPLE GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephane Grappelli was a celebrated French jazz violinist, partner of Django Reinhardt.

clue.text: Good collar for these billy goats?

parts.note: a ruff is a stiff frilled collar worn in Elizabethan times

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a smart collar would suit a group of billy goats.
explanation.walkthrough: The Three Billy Goats Gruff are the goats of the Norwegian fairy tale who outwit the troll under the bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy tale's three goats share the surname Gruff, so it names them.

clue.text: That is Bedlam's version of a Lakeland bottleneck

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworked form of it, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
the word Bedlam with its S kept as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A chaotic madhouse is offered as a picture of a traffic jam in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the S of 'Bedlam's' counts as a letter, joining IE and BEDLAM in the mix. Ambleside is a Lake District town notorious for traffic congestion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambleside, a town in the English Lake District, sits where several roads meet and is famous for traffic jams.

clue.text: Discussion between sessions of Congress?

parts.note: congress also means sexual intercourse, so the chat comes in bed between bouts of lovemaking rather than in the US legislature

explanation.surface: Politicians talk informally during a break in the American legislature.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate conversation in bed between lovers, congress being an old word for sex.

clue.text: Monks' brethren on the Italian rise in relief work

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: John Monks led the TUC, the Trades Union Congress, whose members call each other brothers
taken as written
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Religious brothers join an Italian in rising up to do charitable relief work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monks' looks like religious men, but it is John Monks, general secretary of the Trades Union Congress (TUC) when this appeared. 'rise' turns the whole run TUC ON IL upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A linocut is a print made from a design cut in relief on linoleum.

clue.text: The state of Jones, at home with Artemis in Rome

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
the Roman counterpart of the Greek goddess Artemis was Diana

explanation.surface: Mr Jones relaxes at home with a Greek goddess transplanted to Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Indiana Jones is the film archaeologist; Indiana is also a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a US state and also the first name of the film hero Jones.

clue.text: Society for high scoring marbles contenders

definitions.text: Society for high scoring marbles contenders

parts.words: Society for high scoring marbles contenders
parts.note: marbles means wits, so the high scorers are people who do well in intelligence tests, not players of the playground game

explanation.surface: A club exists for champion players of the game of marbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Mensa is the society whose members must score highly on an IQ test.

clue.text: Many in port cut some ice by telekenesis

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, hence many
taken as written
Dover is the Channel port in Kent
to cut some ice is to matter, to count for something

explanation.surface: Large numbers in a harbour break through ice using the power of thought.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue spells telekinesis as 'telekenesis'. MIND OVER MATTER fills 6 and 13 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Telekinesis is the supposed moving of objects by thought alone, the mind's power over physical things.

clue.text: Simple northern welcome welcoming one

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest in, so one piece goes inside the greeting

parts.note: ave is the Latin greeting hail or welcome
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A plain-spoken northerner gives a warm greeting to a single guest.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive and simple both describe someone artless and unsophisticated.

clue.text: English FA members getting one in the net

indicators.note: the members of English FA are its letters, which make up something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: Players of the English Football Association score a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface makes 'the net' the goal; here it is a fishing net. 'members' asks you to rearrange the letters of ENGLISH FA.
explanation.definitionFit: An angelfish is a brightly coloured tropical fish, the sort caught in a net.

clue.text: Its flowers cluster among chrysanthemum, belladonna etc

indicators.note: among means sitting within other words, so the letters run across chrysanthemum and belladonna

explanation.surface: A list of garden plants describes how blooms bunch together.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbel is a flower cluster whose stalks spread from one point, as in cow parsley.

clue.text: None dying badly without doubt, there's _____

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that nobody dies badly, and fills in the missing phrase themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank at the end is completed by the answer, giving 'without doubt, there's no denying'.
explanation.definitionFit: There is no denying something when it is beyond doubt; the phrase means certainly.

clue.text: Hidden faults among Ali's supporters?

definitions.meaning: weaknesses concealed in someone admired, from the statue with clay feet in the Book of Daniel
Muhammad Ali was born Cassius Clay, and his feet supported him

explanation.surface: Concealed weaknesses are found among the fans of a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporters' suggests fans; it means feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Feet of clay is an idiom for an unsuspected weakness in a respected person.

clue.text: Prime minister said to be candid

definitions.meaning: Sir Robert ... was British Prime Minister in the 1830s and 1840s
candid sounds like candied, and candied orange rind is a familiar baking ingredient

explanation.surface: A head of government is reported to be refreshingly frank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'candid' is said like 'candied', and the rind so described is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Peel founded the Metropolitan Police and served twice as Prime Minister.

clue.text: See 6
Peter James's valet and sometime chamber body

parts.note: Peter Quint is the dead valet who haunts Henry James's The Turn of the Screw
et is French and Latin for and

explanation.surface: A novelist's manservant once belonged to a chamber group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter James' looks like a crime novelist; it is Peter, the valet in a story by Henry James.
explanation.definitionFit: A quintet is a group of five players, a usual chamber music ensemble.

clue.text: Fox's way to question 'is maker, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A fox asks itself in dialect whether it is a creator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fox' is George Fox, founder of the Society of Friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Quakerism is the religious movement founded by George Fox in the 17th century.

clue.text: Old Left in a live broadcast: such should aid their aspirations…

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Old left-wingers appear in a live broadcast, hoping it will help their ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges A LIVE into ALVEI, and 'in' puts OL inside it. 'aspirations' looks like ambitions but means breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: Alveoli are the tiny air sacs in the lungs where breathing exchanges gases.

clue.text: Good testosterone, but no trial to discern her response to it!

indicators.note: to discern the answer the remaining letters must be sorted out into a fresh order
but no means without, so a stretch of letters is taken away

parts.note: a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A woman's reaction to the male hormone is judged good without any experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove TEST from TESTOSTERONE to leave OSTERONE, add G and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Oestrogen is the main female sex hormone, the counterpart to male testosterone.

clue.text: … and are Old Left taking a bearing in pinkish circles?

parts.note: taken as written
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Elderly left-wingers take their bearings among pink rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Areolae are the pink or brown rings of skin around nipples.

clue.text: Athene on rising takes morning for hot flushes

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the result is read upwards
takes one thing for another means swaps it in, replacing a letter

explanation.surface: A goddess rises in the morning suffering from hot flushes.
explanation.walkthrough: In ATHENE swap H for AM to give ATAMENE, and 'on rising' turns that upwards. 'flushes' are not the menopausal kind but washings out.
explanation.definitionFit: Enemata, the plural of enema, are injections of fluid that flush out the bowel.

clue.text: Right to fail in British school's Russian course

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Sch is the abbreviation for school

indicators.note: something that fails breaks down, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A British school claims the right to fail its pupils in Russian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a course of study, given the British school, but it is a course of a meal. Bortsch is the beetroot soup of Russia and Eastern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Bortsch, or borscht, is the beetroot soup served as a course in Russia.

clue.text: The little woman's going out with trash: give her a ring!

indicators.note: going out with means surrounding, the outer piece wraps round the other

parts.note: Beth is one of the four sisters in Little Women
rot means rubbish or trash

explanation.surface: A man's girlfriend is going out with a worthless type, so he hurries to propose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The little woman' looks like a wife; it is Beth March of Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: To betroth is to engage someone to marry, the ring being the sign.

clue.text: Bearing slash from sword

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing
slash is slang for urinating

explanation.surface: A fencer takes a bearing and cuts with a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slash' looks like a sword cut; it is British slang for a pee.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is a thrusting sword used in fencing.

clue.text: Message from Gallagher: 'e's making a comeback!

indicators.note: making a comeback means turning back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: Liam Gallagher is the singer of Oasis
'e is the dropped-h form of he

explanation.surface: Liam Gallagher sends word that his band is reforming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' turns LIAM E backwards. Oasis did reform, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-mail is a message sent electronically.

clue.text: One's in the field to put Eton's opponents on hold

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts one piece after another

parts.note: a rest is a support or hold
Harrow is the public school that is Eton's traditional rival

explanation.surface: A schoolboy delays a match against Eton's old rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton and Harrow are famous English boarding schools and old rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Restharrow is a wild plant of fields whose tough roots once stopped the harrow.

clue.text: Invertebrates' diet

parts.note: suggests what spineless creatures eat, but a Diet is an assembly, and the famous one met in a German city that shares its name with creeping invertebrates

explanation.surface: A question about what spineless animals eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Diet of Worms of 1521 was the assembly that condemned Martin Luther.

clue.text: Successive notes from Gustave

parts.note: do is the first note of the sol-fa scale
re follows do in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A man called Gustave plays two notes one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustave Doré was the French artist famous for his Bible and Dante engravings.

clue.text: Flame cutting into the moutarde?

annotationWithheld.why: Flame cutting into the moutarde? (9) for INAMORATO: 'Flame' defines it, but no reading of 'cutting into the moutarde' builds the letters, and no source gives the parse

clue.text: Woods burning with fearful symmetry?

definitions.meaning: Blake's poem has the beast burning bright with fearful symmetry

explanation.surface: Forests are ablaze in an alarming, balanced pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woods' looks like forests; it is the golfer's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger is Woods's first name, and Blake's Tyger is the beast of fearful symmetry.

clue.text: AA member on line, perhaps?

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for member, as in MBE

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A motoring organisation's patrolman is reached on the phone line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'AA' looks like the Automobile Association; it is the initials of the author of Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne was the English author of Winnie-the-Pooh, known by his initials.

clue.text: They stick to nasty head wounds

indicators.note: nasty suggests damage, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: rents are tears or rips

explanation.surface: Dressings cling to unpleasant gashes on the scalp.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherents stick to a cause or leader as loyal supporters.
